valuation.method: Forward EPS x P/E: FY2027 adjusted diluted EPS (viewed at the 12-month target date, Nov 2026 to Nov 2027) times a justified P/E. Listing is the US common share, USD, no ADR conversion. FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance $15.20-$15.30 (Q3 reported $4.86; Q4 guide $3.40-$3.50, includes ~$0.10 tax headwind); FY2027 EPS is my own assumption from organic growth, margin and buybacks, not company guidance.

bear.driver: Data-center/commercial orders slow after record $12.5B backlog converts; margin pressure persists; EPS growth only ~6% off the FY2026 guide midpoint

base.driver: Backlog (+73% y/y) converts, organic growth high single digit, modest margin expansion and buybacks give ~13% EPS growth over the FY2026 guide midpoint ($15.25)

bull.driver: Data-center cooling demand sustains double-digit organic growth with margin gains; premium multiple holds

valuation.implied_by_close: At base EPS $17.30 the close of $386.29 implies 22.3x; the equal-weighted named target of about $515 implies 29.8x, or EPS about $21.5 at the base 24x (about 24% above the model).
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $17.30 (4.5 pp of the close).
valuation.watch_metric: Organic orders and backlog conversion in Commercial HVAC (data-center share), and adjusted EPS vs the FY2026 $15.20-$15.30 guide and initial FY2027 guide
valuation.next_disclosure: Q4/FY2026 earnings release, expected around late Jan to early Feb 2027 (date not confirmed)

analyst_notes: All sourced named calls since the Oct 29 release are target cuts with Buy-equivalent ratings kept (Evercore 565 to 560, Oppenheimer 530 to 500, RBC 496 to 486, Citi 566 to 549, JPMorgan 550 to 480), so cuts and bullish ratings coexist; the stock fell from about $418 to $386 in the week to the close, which raises implied upside beyond the revisions. The roughly $515 average of these five is about 24% above the base model, equivalent to ~30x FY2027 EPS or ~$21.5 EPS at 24x. Analyst names and exact dates for UBS, Baird, Mizuho, Argus, Bernstein and Goldman were not verifiable, so they are excluded; the sample is five firms, mostly one week old, and dividend of $4.20 uses Yahoo's indicated rate.
